0.headline: Flood of IPOs: 16 public issues to hit Dalal Street next week, 9 listings scheduled
0.heading: Flood of IPOs: 16 public issues to hit Dalal Street next week, 9 listings scheduled
0.intro: Including the September issues, the total fundraising through IPOs in the current calendar year has reached nearly Rs 87,900 crore.
0.body:
Investors will see a flood of IPOs next week, starting September 7, with 16 companies hitting Dalal Street with their maiden public issues to raise more than Rs 7,300 crore, despite subdued equity market conditions amid tensions in West Asia and elevated oil prices.

The list of 16 companies includes 12 initial public offerings (IPOs) worth around Rs 7,200 crore from the mainboard segment.

Including the September issues, the total fundraising through IPOs in the current calendar year has reached nearly Rs 87,900 crore.

September 7
Mumbai-based real estate developer Pranav Constructions will be the first mainboard company to launch its IPO, opening its Rs 351-crore maiden public issue on September 7. The price band has been fixed at Rs 118-124 per share.

Logistics services provider Apana Logistics, from the SME segment, will also open its IPO on the same day, seeking to raise Rs 34 crore at a fixed issue price of Rs 60 per share. Both issues will close on September 9.

September 8
This will be followed by three mainboard IPOs — Kanohar Electricals, Prasol Chemicals, and Glass Wall Systems (India) — all of which will open on September 8 and close on September 10.

Transformer manufacturer Kanohar Electricals has tapped the capital markets to raise Rs 1,055.7 crore at the upper end of its price band of Rs 601-632 per share.

Specialty chemicals maker Prasol Chemicals has fixed its price band at Rs 643-676 per share for its Rs 500-crore IPO.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Façade solutions and fenestration provider Glass Wall Systems (India) is raising Rs 428 crore through its IPO, with a price band of Rs 172-182 per share.

September 9
The maximum number of IPOs next week will open on September 9, with six from the mainboard segment — Rentomojo, Asset Reconstruction Company (India), Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions, Steamhouse India, LCC Projects, and Karamtara Engineering — and three from the SME segment — Amtech Esters, Vinod Texworld, and Infrax Renewable.

Together, these nine IPOs will raise Rs 4,611 crore, accounting for around 64 percent of the total fundraising next week.

Rentomojo, a technology-driven direct-to-consumer online rental and subscription platform for furniture and appliances in India, will be the largest among them, mobilising Rs 1,256 crore at a price band of Rs 384-404 per share.

Payment cards manufacturer Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions is raising Rs 805 crore at the upper end of its price band of Rs 322-339 per share.

Karamtara Engineering, a manufacturer of products for the renewable energy and transmission sectors, is looking to raise Rs 875 crore through its IPO, with a price band of Rs 241-254 per share.

The IPO of Asset Reconstruction Company (India) will fetch Rs 733 crore at the higher end of its price band of Rs 132-139 per share. It will be the first asset reconstruction company to list on Dalal Street.

Gujarat-based industrial gas supplier Steamhouse India has tapped the capital markets to raise up to Rs 414 crore through its IPO, while LCC Projects, which provides engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) services for irrigation and water supply projects, is mobilising Rs 427 crore at the upper end of its price band of Rs 139-146 per share.

In the SME segment, textile company Vinod Texworld is looking to raise nearly Rs 43 crore through a fixed-price issue at Rs 94 per share.

Solar energy company Infrax Renewable aims to raise Rs 40.88 crore at a fixed price of Rs 104 per share.

Chemical manufacturing company Amtech Esters will raise Rs 17.88 crore at the upper end of its price band of Rs 71-75 per share.

September 10
Kerala-based real estate company Veegaland Developers will tap the capital markets on September 10 to raise Rs 210 crore through an IPO, comprising entirely a fresh issue of shares. The price band has been fixed at Rs 130-140 per share.

September 11
Plastics products manufacturer Manika Plastech will be the last company to open its IPO next week, on September 11.

The company has not disclosed its price band, and therefore, the total issue size is not available. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 92.5 crore, along with an offer for sale (OFS) of 76.74 lakh shares by promoter entity VRIDAA Holding Trust.

IPOs Closing Next Week
Meanwhile, Qualiance International's Rs 45-crore IPO will close on September 8. The public issue received a strong response from investors on September 4, the first day of bidding, when it was subscribed 12.51 times.

Nine Listings Scheduled Next Week
A total of nine new companies will be available for trading on the bourses next week, including three from the mainboard segment.

Luxury fashion company Purple Style Labs will list its shares on the stock exchanges on September 7, followed by Rays of Belief, the parent company of MOM's Belief, and gold and diamond jewellery maker Deepa Jewellers on September 8.

In the SME segment, Ashutosh Fibre and Shanti Inorganics will make their debut on the NSE Emerge platform, while Phychem Technologies will list on the BSE SME platform on September 7.

Fly-Hi Maritime Travels and Farm Peace are expected to list on the BSE SME platform on September 8.

Qualiance International will be the last company to list next week, with its shares likely to make their debut on the NSE Emerge platform on September 11.

1.headline: West Asia conflict, crude oil prices, US inflation data to steer stock market: Analysts
1.heading: West Asia conflict, crude oil prices, US inflation data to steer stock market: Analysts
1.intro: On the domestic front, investors will continue to monitor foreign institutional flows, the rupee, crude oil prices and domestic liquidity
1.body:
Developments in the West Asia conflict, crude oil prices, and US inflation data would be the major drivers for the stock market next week, according to analysts.

Besides, trading activities of foreign investors and global market trends will also influence domestic equities.

"This week is expected to remain highly sensitive to global monetary policy, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments. Investors will closely monitor the impact of the stronger-than-expected US employment data on expectations regarding the Federal Reserve's September policy decision," Ajit Mishra – SVP, Research, Religare Broking Ltd, said.

On the domestic front, investors will continue to monitor foreign institutional flows, the rupee, crude oil prices and domestic liquidity, he added.

"Developments around the Strait of Hormuz will also remain a critical monitorable given their implications for India's inflation, external balance and corporate profitability," Mishra noted.

Brent crude gained more than 8 per cent during the week, while WTI crude rose over 9 per cent, as renewed US-Iran hostilities and concerns surrounding the Strait of Hormuz increased the geopolitical risk premium in global energy markets, Ponmudi R, CEO – Enrich Money, an online trading and wealth tech firm, said.

"With the latest US jobs data coming in stronger-than-expected and pointing to resilient underlying economic momentum, attention now shifts to the upcoming US inflation data, which could prove critical in shaping expectations for Federal Reserve policy and global market sentiment.

"The direction of Treasury yields and interest-rate expectations will remain closely intertwined with the inflation narrative, while elevated oil prices amid the unresolved Middle East conflict are likely to remain a persistent overhang on market sentiment," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of HST Wealth, a Research Analyst firm, said.

Last week, the 30-share BSE Sensex declined 749.08 points, or 0.96 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty fell 277.95 points, or 1.14 per cent.

"Indian equity markets remained volatile and under pressure during the week, with the Nifty-50 extending its losing streak to four consecutive weeks, the longest such stretch in five months, as intensifying US-Iran hostilities drove a sharp surge in crude oil prices and kept risk sentiment firmly on edge," Ponmudi said.

Global markets enter the week facing a familiar set of challenges, with the outlook hinging on US monetary-policy expectations, elevated crude oil prices and the evolving geopolitical situation in West Asia, he added.

2.headline: 11 IPOs worth Rs 7,055 crore to hit D-Street next week; Rentomojo, Karamtara among key issues
2.heading: 11 IPOs worth Rs 7,055 crore to hit D-Street next week; Rentomojo, Karamtara among key issues
2.intro: The IPOs are scheduled to hit the market between September 7 and September 15, with most of the issues opening for subscription on Tuesday and Wednesday
2.body:
India's primary market is bracing for another packed week, with 11 main-board companies — including Rentomojo, Karamtara Engineering and Kanohar Electricals — set to raise Rs 7,055 crore through initial public offerings (IPOs).

The IPOs are scheduled to open between September 7 and September 15, with most issues launching for subscription on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"This multi-issue rush reflects an eagerness to lock in early-stage growth equity in young companies as all these companies are below USD 1 billion market cap at listing," said Rajkumar Rathi, Chief Investment Officer at YES Securities.

The companies heading to the primary market span real estate development, engineering and manufacturing, payments and identity solutions, specialty chemicals, and online rental services.

Of the total Rs 7,055 crore, Rs 2,722 crore (39 per cent) constitutes primary capital issuance, where proceeds go directly to the companies, while Rs 4,333 crore (61 per cent) represents a secondary sale by existing shareholders. This split, Rathi noted, reflects strong corporate confidence and ample liquidity within India's primary market.

Proceeds from the fresh issues will primarily be used for business expansion, capital expenditure, debt repayment, working capital needs and other general corporate purposes.

The upcoming wave of IPOs follows an already active start to September, with Rays of Belief and Deepa Jewellers launching their issues on September 1. With this latest batch, the total number of companies launching IPOs in 2026 is expected to climb to 75 — which includes 23 issues launched in August.

Among the 11 companies, Pranav Constructions will be the first to open for public subscription on September 7. The issue, worth over Rs 351 crore, will close on September 9.

It will be followed by Kanohar Electricals, Prasol Chemicals and Glass Wall Systems (India), which open their IPOs on September 8. Rentomojo, Manipal Payment and Identity Solutions, Arcil, LCC Projects, Karamtara Engineering and Steamhouse India will launch their issues on September 9, while Veegaland Developers will open its IPO on September 10.

Pranav Constructions has set a price band of Rs 118-124 per share, comprising a fresh issue worth Rs 315.6 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 28.57 lakh shares valued at Rs 35.43 crore.

Kanohar Electricals has fixed a price band of Rs 601-632 per share for its Rs 1,056-crore issue.

Prasol Chemicals' price band stands at Rs 643-676 per share for its Rs 500-crore IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 80 crore and an OFS of up to Rs 420 crore.

Glass Wall Systems (India) has set a price band of Rs 172-182 per share for its Rs 428-crore issue.

Rentomojo has fixed its price band at Rs 384-404 per equity share for a Rs 1,256-crore IPO, comprising a fresh issue worth up to Rs 150 crore and an OFS of 2.73 crore shares valued at Rs 1,106 crore at the upper price band.

Karamtara Engineering's Rs 875-crore IPO includes a fresh issue of Rs 675 crore and an OFS worth up to Rs 200 crore, with a price band of Rs 241-254 per share.

Manipal Payment and Identity Solutions has set a price band of Rs 322-339 per share for its Rs 805-crore issue, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 320 crore and an OFS of up to 1.43 crore shares worth Rs 485 crore.

Arcil's Rs 733-crore IPO, priced at Rs 132-139 per share, is entirely an OFS — meaning the company will not receive any proceeds from the offering.

LCC Projects has fixed a price band of Rs 139-146 per share for its Rs 427-crore issue.

Steamhouse India aims to raise Rs 414 crore through its IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 353 crore and an OFS of Rs 61 crore.

Veegaland Developers will raise Rs 210 crore entirely through a fresh issue of shares, with its IPO opening on September 10 and closing on September 15.

With PTI inputs
